validated_10um_minimum.mirror_degeneracy_note: The one-electrode radial pattern is reflection-symmetric about its radial axis; equal-radius minima on the two sides are physically expected and optimizer signs may differ.
validated_10um_minimum.interpretation_limit: A nonzero minimum of the 4-component quadrature field norm is an effective-potential minimum, not an exact RF null. It is the lowest location found by the disclosed grid and multi-start methods in r<=5 mm; the finite grid does not prove a mathematical global minimum.

field_mesh_sensitivity.changed_geometry_comparison: direct full-domain P4 h35 versus h50 for the same +10 um radial displacement of electrode 0
field_mesh_sensitivity.nominal_comparison: existing FEM-derived N48 h35 versus h50 on nominal geometry only; N48 is never used to represent a displaced geometry
field_mesh_sensitivity.samples: same 144 deterministic azimuth points on radii 0.5 to 7 mm; no angular interpolation

local_minima_and_saddles.known_local_minima: At 10 um radial outward, the previous multi-start validation found the global mirror-related pair near radius 0.44581 mm and a higher local-minimum basin near radius 0.45811 mm along the electrode axis.
local_minima_and_saddles.saddle_and_barrier_status: Not established by the existing files. A local extremum of the quadrature-field norm is an effective-potential stationary point, not an exact RF null. Mesh-piecewise field gradients make unverified local Hessians/barrier heights unreliable.

claim_limit: The exponent near one third is compatible with balancing a displacement-induced approximately constant dipolar electric field against an ideal octupolar field proportional to r^3; four amplitudes do not prove the asymptotic law or a fabrication tolerance.
